title: Wild Bill Donovan and the original crash-retrieval protocols

tellings.quote: Chief OSS member and another CIA founder, Wild Bill Donovan, who journalist Chris Sharp notes was likely not only involved in the Magenta crash retrieval, but in setting up original protocols for UFO crash retrievals, was also a Knight of Malta.

plain: William "Wild Bill" Donovan, head of the OSS, the US wartime spy agency that came before the CIA, and one of the CIA's founders, is said to have helped recover a crashed craft near Magenta, in Italy, and to have written the first rules for recovering crashed UFOs. Michels tells this himself, crediting the journalist Chris Sharp. He adds that Donovan was a Knight of Malta, a member of an old Catholic order of knights. If true, it would mean secret recoveries of crashed craft started well before the end of the Second World War.
